title: OpenAI reusable prompts deprecation, Salesforce connection security changes, and more app updates
text: OpenAI reusable prompts deprecation, Salesforce connection security changes, and more app updates. Release notes 2026 OpenAI reusable prompts deprecation, Salesforce connection security changes, and more app updates 6 min Here's a quick look at our app updates this week. OpenAI: Reusable prompts deprecation and new GPT-6.2 models Reusable prompts in the OpenAI app stop working on November 30, 2026. The app also now supports the GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models. Reusable prompts deprecation Update your scenarios before November 30, 2026. After this date, OpenAI shuts down its reusable prompts API ( v1/prompts ), and scenarios that use it stop running. This change affects the Generate a response module when Prompt Type is set to Reusable prompt . These options are now labeled Reusable prompt (deprecated) . Existing scenarios continue to run normally until the deadline. To keep your scenarios running: Identify scenarios that use the Generate a response module with Prompt Type set to Reusable prompt (deprecated) . In your OpenAI account, copy the text from the reusable prompt you use. In your scenario, edit the module and change Prompt Type to Text prompt or Advanced input . Paste the prompt text directly into the module's configuration. For more information, see OpenAI documentation and OpenAI's guide to migrating from prompt objects . Support for GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol These modules now support the GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models: Simple text prompt : You can select the new models if you're on a paid Make plan. Generate a completion and Analyze images : Make automatically omits the n parameter (number of choices to generate) when you use these models to ensure compatibility. title: Introducing the Make plugin for Claude
text: Introducing the Make plugin for Claude. Release notes 2026 Introducing the Make plugin for Claude 2 min You can now use the Make plugin for Claude to turn your recurring work in Claude into Make scenarios. Describe the work in plain language, then create, schedule, run, and manage it through your existing Make account. Key benefits Create scenarios: Describe a workflow in Claude, and Make creates the scenario, connects to the required apps, and runs it. Schedule and run scenarios: Set scenarios to run on a schedule, or run them on demand from Claude. Review scenario activity: Search scenarios by name, folder, or status. View scenario run history and past results in interactive Claude widgets. Manage everything in Make: The plugin uses your existing Make account permissions. Scenarios, connections, and stored data stay in your Make organization, where your teams can review and manage them. Install the Make plugin for Claude To install the plugin, open the Make listing in the Anthropic Claude plugin directory and add the plugin to Claude. Availability The plugin is available for Claude users on all Make plans. Use it in Claude Chat, Claude Cowork, and Claude Code. Learn more To see what the community is saying, see Make plugin for Claude feature spotlight . title: From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity
text: From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity. November 25, 2026 Science From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity Robert Brunck, Stefan Ganscha, Swaroop Guntupalli, Dariusz Lasecki, Gabriella Marfani, Jack Mason, Hussain Masoom, Rose Mirshafian, Eliseo Papa and Zoi Tsangalidou Explore Science on Google Antigravity Share Built in collaboration with analytical chemists and using community-developed tools, Mass Spec Skills empowers scientists using Google Antigravity to interpret tandem mass spectra, lay out chemical evidence, and match frontier-level retrieval accuracy even with a lightweight model. Every sample of blood, soil or plant tissue contains a vast array of small molecules, such as nutrients, hormones, drugs and their breakdown products, pollutants, or bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential. A modern mass spectrometer can detect tens of thousands of these molecular signals in a single drop of sample extract, measuring the masses of charged molecules and, in tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS), the fragments they break into. These measurements, however, do not directly reveal the molecular structure. Researchers cannot immediately tell which compound produced a signal and relate it to its biological role or downstream use cases. To fully map the diversity of small molecules, which remains largely uncharted, researchers need ways to translate mass spectra to molecular structures at scale. The standard approach is to match each spectrum against reference spectra from previously measured molecules. title: Migrating our Messages API to Rust
text: Migrating our Messages API to Rust. 01 Why migrate? Related articles Effective harnesses for long-running agents View more Many problems have a generator–verifier gap: it’s often far easier to verify that a solution is correct than to come up with one. Sudoku is a classic example. It’s simple to check the solution (just count the numbers in each row, column, and box), but finding that solution can take a long time. Many ambitious Claude projects have relied on this gap: formalizing proofs in mathematics or migrating large, well-tested codebases are tasks Claude can take on as long as it has a reliable way to verify its work. But as Claude has become more capable, it’s begun to take on projects in live systems, where generating the work is easier than verifying it. In these systems, users often rely on edge cases and quirks that fall outside the test suite , and it’s hard to write a definition of “correct” that covers everything . Without a reliable way to check Claude’s work, the migration of a live system is hard to trust—however quickly Claude can generate the code for it. We ran into this problem when we migrated our Messages API from Python to Rust. This API is the primary way that customers—as well as our own apps, like Claude Code and Cowork—reach Claude. From early 2024 to fall 2026, API traffic grew roughly 1,800 times. Rust would allow us to use far less CPU per request. Claude wrote a first version of the API’s core request path in about a week. But building trust in the migration required us to find a way to verify that our Rust API was at parity with our production API. title: November 23, 2026
text: November 23, 2026. Skip to navigation November 23, 2026 November 23, 2026 Swift SDK v4 Swift SDK v4.0.0 is the first stable release of the redesigned SDK for ElevenAgents conversations, and the core ElevenLabs library now follows semantic versioning. One ConversationClient runs any number of conversations, starting voice conversations over WebRTC with startVoiceConversation and text-only conversations over a WebSocket with startTextOnlyConversation , each with credentials matched to its transport at compile time. Client tools registered in clientTools send their own results, chatHistory updates streamed replies in place, and onDisconnect reports why a conversation ended. The v4.0.0 release notes list every change and link a migration guide from v3. Agents as code ElevenAgents agents can now be defined in code with the Agent builder in the Python and JavaScript SDKs, from v2.80.0. One definition holds the agent’s settings, its tools and its workflow, and agents.push() creates or updates the agent and every webhook and client tool it uses, filling in the tool IDs and leaving unchanged tools alone. agents.pull() and AgentProject keep agents in the same project layout as the ElevenLabs CLI, and validate() checks an agent in CI without an API key. See Agents as code . New agent LLMs ElevenAgents adds four LLMs: GPT-6.2 Sol ( gpt-6.2-sol ), GPT-6.2 Astra ( gpt-6.2-astra ), Gemini 4 Hydrogen ( gemini-4-hydrogen ) and Gemini 4 Neon ( gemini-4-neon ). Select them in the agent’s LLM picker or set them as llm through the API. The GPT-6.2 models and Gemini 4 Neon run at low reasoning effort unless the agent sets one. text: Claude Code v2.1.332 published 2026-11-25. ## What's changed - Added skills from MCP servers (beta).
